meanings: verb: to go back to a previous position
examples: Before a tsunami hits, the water recedes, which is dangerous for those who unknowingly go to investigate before the big waves come rushing in.

meanings: noun: a highly valued object from a very long time ago
examples: Among the relics held in Notre Dame cathedral is a piece of wood believed to be part of the cross on which Jesus died.

meanings: verb: to spread widely, create more of
examples: Copernicus first wrote that the earth revolved around the sun, but it was Galileo who later propagated the idea to wider audience.

meanings: noun: an incorrect idea that somebody believes strongly
examples: I think his dream of living in wealthy Beverly Hills is a delusion, but he continues to tell people that is where he will be living in a year.

meanings: verb: to completely separate in all directions
examples: Three days after I accidentally cooked a mouse that had crawled into my oven, the smell still hasn't dissipated.

meanings: adjective: causing harm or injury
examples: Many know that smoking is detrimental to your health, but processed sugar in large quantities is equally bad.

meanings: adjective: requiring a lot of physical effort
examples: One of the most strenuous races on earth, the Ironman Triathlon requires swimming 2.4 miles, biking 112 miles, and then running a marathon.

meanings: adjective: similar in some respects but otherwise different
examples: There are few animals that form partnerships analogous to marriage, but among them are eagles, wolves, and even some fish.

meanings: noun: a promised reward to motivate
examples: Tom knew none of his friends would help him move to his new house without an incentive, so he promised to buy everybody pizza at the end of the day.

meanings: adjective: not sharp
examples: The blunt knife can't cut the bread—it barely can cut the butter!

meanings: verb: to explore and learn about using hands or a tool
examples: The new camera is designed to probe the interiors of blood vessels, giving a detailed view that doctors have never had before now.

meanings: noun: a person who has a role after a previous person
examples: US President James Buchanan didn't know what to do when the US Civil War started, but fortunately his successor, Abraham Lincoln, was a wise leader.

meanings: verb: to go up and down regularly in amount
examples: While the light of the Sun appears constant from day to day, the light of the Moon fluctuates over the course of a month.

meanings: verb: to move very near an acceptable limit
examples: The US President's ability to give military orders without declaring war encroaches on the Congress's authority in giving the formal declaration.

meanings: adjective: complete and very detailed
examples: Wikipedia makes no claim to be an exhaustive encyclopedia, as many more obscure topics don't even have pages.

meanings: adjective: secret or hidden
examples: The attack was intended to be covert, but before it could begin, the entire plan was revealed to the target.

meanings: adjective: with careful attention to details
examples: Overconfident students may understand how to solve math problems but not be meticulous in their calculations, resulting in wrong answers.

meanings: adjective: able to change; changing frequently
examples: Robin Williams was a dynamic comedian: because of his sharp mind and ability to improvise, even his co-actors didn't know what he might say next.

meanings: adjective: lasting a very short time
examples: If we lived forever and life was not transitory, do you think we would appreciate life less or more?

meanings: verb: to attract or persuade with promises of benefits
examples: Some of the most effective hunters are those who entice their targets into traps with the appearance or smell of food.

meanings: noun: a small sickness or cause of physical discomfort
examples: At the age of 80, my grandfather is lucky to have no major illness and struggle with only a small number of minor ailments.

meanings: verb: to cut from a hard material
examples: With careful strokes of a sharp blade, the sculptor carved his beautiful statue from a single piece of wood.

meanings: adjective: of the countryside; simple and old-fashioned
examples: The artist was known for painting rustic landscapes since there were always cows and farms in his pictures.

meanings: adjective: fake or untrue (generally of illegal claims)
examples: Since I have no background in medicine, If I advertised my services as a doctor, I'd soon be arrested for making the fraudulent claim.

meanings: verb: to produce a liquid (from or within a living thing)
examples: Saliva is created in the mouth constantly, but it is secreted most rapidly when eating or drinking.

meanings: noun: a person or thing with the same function as another in a different place
examples: Years after the war in Vietnam, General Westmoreland of the American Army criticized the strategies of his counterpart from the North, General Giap.

meanings: adjective: acting as a key part of a process
examples: The university believed that passion was instrumental to learning—without it, you'd be wasting your time in class.

meanings: verb: to win completely in a competition or fight
examples: Modern medicine has nearly vanquished some diseases that only two generations ago might have been deadly.

meanings: noun: something that is not normal, standard, or expected
examples: After finding anomalies in the data from her experiment on the effects of caffeine on turtles, Anne decided to start again.

meanings: adjective: required by rule
examples: Although she had always hated writing, Mary found that the compulsory Intro to Writing class taught her valuable skills.

meanings: adjective: comfortable when talking to other people
examples: Dave is outgoing and confident nowadays, especially at parties, but few know that he struggled with social anxiety earlier in life.

meanings: verb: to care for lovingly
examples: Although it was far less beautiful than her more expensive clothing, Leah cherished the dress her mother had made by hand.

meanings: adjective: able to see the most important information to make a decision
examples: Alfonzo was an astute chess player, always ready to use an opponent's misplay as an opportunity to attack.

meanings: adjective: with strong images or colors
examples: In its famous baptism scene, the movie The Godfather showed a vivid contrast between the peace of a church and bloody murders of gang rivals.

meanings: adjective: very serious
examples: Most of Bach's orchestral melodies are light, but his organ music often has a grave quality that fits movie scenes of suspense or horror.

meanings: verb: to try hard to achieve something
examples: Every day he strives to be on time to work, but despite his honest efforts, he is late more often than not.

meanings: verb: to ask for emotionally, to beg
examples: Crying, the new driver pleaded with the officer not to give her a speeding ticket, but he refused to listen, his face emotionless.

meanings: noun: the time of evening before complete darkness
examples: The brightest handful of stars first become visible at twilight, but most stars stay hidden until the full darkness of night has fallen.

meanings: noun: to suddenly move or push hard
examples: When the traffic light turned green, all of Mike's passengers suddenly felt a jolt as he pushed his foot down hard on the gas pedal.

meanings: adjective: slanted, higher at one end and lower at the other
examples: Most houses in Canada have sloping roofs because the weight of snow on a flat roof could destroy a house.

meanings: adjective: not real, based on an illusion
examples: You think you may see water in the distance in a desert, but it is only an illusory effect created by the hot layer of air over the sand.

meanings: verb: to come together into a crowd
examples: As the protestor spoke, she drew more and more listeners, who slowly congregated around her to show support for her cause

meanings: adjective: completely impossible, ridiculous
examples: Although it may be ridiculous today to believe the earth is flat, it's even more preposterous to think that the sky is a physical blue disc.

meanings: verb: to confuse somebody
examples: Even skilled mathematicians are sometimes perplexed by physics, since the logic comes not from abstract rules but from the physical world.

meanings: adjective: ordinary and boring
examples: Although Jane knew being a lawyer would pay well, it seemed too mundane, so she left law school to pursue dreams of becoming a celebrity chef.

meanings: adjective: with very little color
examples: The cover of the book was originally bright red, but it became a pale pink after sitting in the sun for three months.

meanings: verb: to add to the end
examples: Mozart, dissatisfied with the tragic, destructive ending to his opera Don Giovanni, appended a final scene that gives a lighter conclusion.

meanings: adjective: long and boring
examples: When asked to memorize every capital city in the world, Michael didn't understand why his teacher had asked him to do such a tedious task.

meanings: noun: extreme tiredness from too much work
examples: The three-day hula-hooping contest left even the most experienced hula hoopers limp with fatigue.

meanings: verb: to cause to happen
examples: Staring at the small screen of a smartphone while on a car or train can induce headaches and motion sickness.
